response.goal: Two-way sync of contacts between HubSpot and our PostgreSQL users table, ensuring new signups appear in HubSpot within 5 minutes, lifecycle stage changes are written back, conflicts are resolved by most recent update and logged, and the solution runs on our server with a README for maintenance.

plan.step: Kickoff and analysis of HubSpot and PostgreSQL schemas
Build inbound sync for new PostgreSQL signups to HubSpot within 5 minutes
Build outbound sync for HubSpot lifecycle stage changes back to PostgreSQL
Implement conflict resolution logic where the most recent update wins with full logging
Deploy to client server and provide a short README for developer maintenance

milestones.name: Milestone 1: Core Sync Logic
milestones.deliverable: Inbound and outbound contact sync between HubSpot and PostgreSQL

milestones.name: Milestone 2: Conflict Resolution, Logging, and Deployment
milestones.deliverable: Conflict resolution with logging, server deployment, and maintenance README

risks.risk: Rate limits on HubSpot API during high volume syncs
risks.mitigation: Implement batching, exponential backoff, and robust error handling in the script.

risks.risk: Timestamp discrepancies between HubSpot server time and PostgreSQL database time
risks.mitigation: Standardize all comparisons using UTC timestamps for accurate most-recent-update win logic.

questions: What specific hosting environment or server OS will the script be deployed on?

assumptions: The client will provide necessary API credentials and database access for HubSpot and PostgreSQL.
The PostgreSQL users table has a recognizable timestamp column for tracking updates.
